thread:
Amy: Hey team — AcmeHealth POC update. Auditor asked for: 1) data-flow cartography (which services touch PHI), 2) list of in-scope infra/components for SOC2/ISO, 3) signed pen-test letter (who can sign?), 4) on-prem SSL cert details (can we share CN/issuer or cert thumbprint only?), and 5) impact to Dedicated pricing if they want staging capacity. They want this by next Tue EOD. Any immediate blockers?

Raj: I can put together a network-diagram + SG/NSG rules. Do they need VPC peering/IP ranges called out? Also: do they want packet-filter level detail or just service-to-service flows?

Amy: Service-to-service flows + CIDR ranges and which subnets are considered "in scope" for the POC. Auditor is ok with high-level diagrams but wants traceability to the assets we list.

Marta (Security): Pen-test letter: security manager can sign a standard attestation, but legal needs to approve any non-standard wording. We typically provide: "Redwood Inference confirms completion of penetration testing engagement on <date> and provides summary of findings; attestation is limited to systems in scope as listed." If AcmeHealth needs the vendor-signed report we can provide either the summary or coordinate an external red-team handoff. Timeline: signed letter available 3 business days after final report.

Chad (Solutions): For Dedicated pricing: if they ask for reserved staging capacity for the POC, that affects monthly commit. We usually recommend ephemeral burst capacity for a 2-week POC to avoid a reserved contract. If they insist on single-tenant hosts for isolation, we need to quote delta (~+25-40% depending on GPU class). I can draft a quick cost split (staging vs prod) once I know requested capacity (vGPU count / QPS).

Amy: Regarding SSL certs: Acme asks for proof certs are managed in-customer KMS for Private deployments. For on-prem POC they want CN and issuer only; do we redact serials/thumbrpints?

Marta (Security): We can provide CN + issuer and certificate transparency logs if public. We do NOT share private keys or full cert chain private data. For KMS integration proof we can provide screenshots of KMS key metadata & CMK thumbprint (redacted) and a short runbook of how keys are rotated. Legal will need to sign off on any screenshot with customer-identifying info.

Raj: Example snippet of the SG rules I'll attach to the diagram (placeholder):
```
- app-subnet (10.10.2.0/24): allow 443 from lb-subnet (10.10.1.0/24)
- db-subnet (10.10.3.0/24): allow 5432 from app-subnet
- peered-acme (172.31.0.0/16): allow 443 from specific host IPs only
```
I'll deliver PNG + exported draw.io XML by EOD today.

Redwood Bot: Uploaded: "pen-test-attestation-template.pdf" to https://drive.redwood.example/attestations/4218765432 (owner: Marta) :white_check_mark:

Marta (Security): I've uploaded a redlined sample pen-test attestation. Legal owns final signature block; Security can sign operational attestation. I'll also prepare a one-page "in-scope assets" list for SOC2 that matches Raj's diagram.

Chad (Solutions): Amy — if we go ephemeral staging, I can add a note in the quote about performance variance and include a small discount for POC. If they want dedicated hosts, I'll need to add a line item for per-GPU reserved fees.

Amy: Great. Action items: Raj -> network diagram + SG rules (EOD today). Marta -> pen-test attestation template + one-page in-scope list (tomorrow). Chad -> POC cost split (ephemeral vs reserved) by EOD. I'll consolidate and send to Acme auditor by Monday morning. Ping me if anything slips.

Marta (Security): Quick heads-up — if the customer asks for vendor-signed full report, we need a signed NDA and consent from our red-team vendor. That adds ~2 business days.

Amy: Noted. Thanks all. :pray:
